---
title: "Chromatin Disruption in Liver Cancer"
description: "How disruption of chromatin regulation drives hepatocellular carcinoma and cholangiocarcinoma."
image: featured.jpg
---

Liver cancer is the third leading cause of cancer death worldwide, and
hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) accounts for most cases. Its incidence continues
to rise, driven by viral hepatitis, metabolic-dysfunction–associated
steatohepatitis, and alcohol-related liver disease. Immune checkpoint inhibitors
are now standard first-line therapy for advanced disease, but fewer than a third
of patients respond and durable benefit is uncommon. Most work on why has
focused on the immune system itself. We focus on a complementary question: how
the chromatin state of the tumor cell determines whether the immune system can
see and kill it.

Chromatin regulators are among the most frequently mutated genes in HCC. The BAF
form of the SWI/SNF remodeling complex alone is disrupted in roughly one in five
liver tumors, defining a large genetic subset with no targeted therapy. In most
other cancers, loss of SWI/SNF makes tumors more visible to the immune system
and more responsive to checkpoint blockade. Liver cancer breaks this pattern. In
our analyses, BAF-mutant tumors have worse survival and do not show the expected
sensitization, which suggests that the liver's tolerant immune environment
reshapes what chromatin disruption means for anti-tumor immunity.

We are defining the chromatin dependencies that BAF-mutant liver tumors rely on
to establish and maintain these altered states, and testing whether disrupting
them can restore anti-tumor immunity. To study this at the real tumor-immune
interface, we pair pooled, epigenome-focused CRISPR screens in immunocompetent
orthotopic liver tumors with T-cell–killing assays using BAF-mutant liver cancer
lines. The aim is to find chromatin regulators whose loss reprograms
immune-response pathways, and to nominate combinations that could make
immunotherapy effective for a molecular subtype of liver cancer with few current
options.
